review_notes: Source-first selection: the central question is whether Big 4 treatment effects reflect client characteristics. The authors emphasize propensity-score matching across three coequal audit-quality proxies; full-sample regression findings are described as indirect support. Retained the full-model propensity-score-matched multivariate families in Tables 2 (ADA), 5 (RPEG), and 8 (ACCY), their separate propensity-logit fits, and the KLW fit required to construct ADA. Excluded unmatched full-sample outcome columns, attribute-specific matched-sample Tables 3/6/9, univariate difference-in-means columns, and later robustness/sensitivity analyses.

Needs review: the paper does not identify the post-exclusion control set in the propensity models; the KLW estimator, per-year/SIC N and aggregate N, and exact ΔSALES operational definition are not reported; RPEG and the exact VAR dispersion statistic lack formulas; ACCY aggregation and ZMIJ inputs are not reported; Equation (4) indexes LOG_MKT and EL at t while their definitions state t+1; the fixed-effect industry coding is unspecified.
results_review_notes: Tables 1, 4, and 7 provide means and standard deviations for retained outcomes and predictors plus the reported raw market-value input to LOG_MKT. Full-sample and matched auditor strata are represented separately; table-level No. Obs. counts are included in group descriptions, not assigned as variable-specific N.

The selected descriptive tables show Big 4 and non-Big 4 sample counts but do not print a separate BIG4 mean or standard deviation; no dummy statistic was calculated. Total Assets rows were excluded because they are not retained baseline variables or a same-time upstream component of a retained predictor.

Current-sweep PDF evidence replaces prior-run PDF citations. Source prose p-value comparison glyphs were resolved by visual inspection of the original PDF; the Table 2 common control statement is strict p<0.01.
